title: Agent Platform for Non-Technical Users
subtitle: Turn multi-channel workflow configuration into versioned, bounded actions with explicit authority and recovery.
author: By Sourav Banerjee

practice_prompts.label: Framing and discovery
practice_prompts.hint: Say why this is a trust problem, ask the five questions and scope out the builder and compiler.

practice_prompts.label: Trace the $500 refund
practice_prompts.hint: Route the Cascade event, name the rule that denies it and why it is refused rather than clamped.

practice_prompts.label: Crash, replay and the two bugs
practice_prompts.hint: Resume after step 0, explain the action key and tell both bugs in order.

practice_prompts.label: Promotion, gaps and week one
practice_prompts.hint: Walk the five stages, name the in-process store gap and close with one safe workflow.

rubric: Frames the round as trust and scopes out the visual builder and NL compiler while naming the spec they must produce.
Separates priority (which workflow should run) from the entity lock (whether two can run at once) with named reasons for no match and lock conflict.
Keeps control flow in a versioned declarative spec and limits the model to typed, validated values.
States the five deny rules in order and refuses the $500 refund under the $50 cap rather than clamping it, keeping the allow-list question separate.
Explains one loop at next_step_index and an action-level idempotency key checked before authorisation, including why cost accounting is a side effect.
Promotes one stage at a time with a non-author approver and names the no-LLM and in-process-store gaps with their production replacements.

editorial_review.evidence: 16 November 2026: re-read all 47 captured sections against the earlier draft section by section. The draft covered the guardrail and gap tables but had dropped or paraphrased away the main questions table's concrete restatements, the non-functional table, the interview shortcut, the nine nouns, u_author_wrong_hat, the 1-apply/1-apply result, the RAG false-alarm link, the $5-vs-$50 note, the three-layer weak/strong argument, the bridge to other cases, the sixty-minute timing table, the six carrying lines and the source two-minute answer (replaced by an authored one); all are restored. The $500 anchor is now its own walkthrough step, the brief defines tenant, canonical event, declarative spec, guardrail and idempotency before use, and each of the eight source figures has a caption and lead naming its actual nodes instead of 'source figure N'. Added reasoning not in the source (effect-before-checkpoint window, args_hash implying fresh authority, event-to-run dedup) is labelled 'Beyond the source'. Broken ', ' allow-row cell fixed; old section-number references rewritten as links. Three source follow-ups (shadow trial, mid-flight stop, cost pivot) added as worked answers 12-14. No RAG specifics transplanted. November 20 complete maintained-baseline review: Complete maintained casebook: brief and case map, ten walkthrough steps, seven diagrams, guardrail and promotion tables, durability, idempotency, gaps, Cascade build and cost deep dives, all practice reveals, the sixty-minute plan and Quick review.
